lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: The reactor is making a noise.

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: It is a reactor. Most of its job is making noises.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: This one sounds expensive.

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: Describe it.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Sort of a clunk, then a hum, then a noise like a cupboard falling down stairs.

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: That is extremely specific.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Is that good?

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: No. But it has saved me a diagnostic cycle.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Should I stop flying?

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: I would stop asking questions before the answer becomes inconvenient.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: The red warning light is blinking now.

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: Which red warning light?

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: The one labelled 'DO NOT IGNORE'.

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: Ah. Marketing insisted on that label.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Should I press anything?

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: Only if it says 'MUTE ALARM'. Even then, emotionally prepare yourself.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Can you talk me through this like I'm in one of those disaster films?

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: In those films they cut away before the paperwork.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: That is not reassuring.

lines.speaker: engineer
lines.text: Neither is the reactor.
